policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV renders the possessive: 'when their hour is come'. The omission leaves only 'the hour', which the ASV does not read.
ASV has an object for the remembering: 'ye may remember them'. The omission leaves the verb absolute, which the ASV does not read.

The added emphatic pronoun is not distinguishable in English: ASV's 'if I go not away' is required by the first-person verb whether or not ego stands with it. The verse note concerns 'Comforter' and is an alternative_rendering.
Emphatic subjunctive negation and simple future negation both yield ASV's 'will not come unto you'; the English does not distinguish them.
ASV reads 'I go to the Father', not 'to my Father'; the added possessive would be rendered and is not.
The candidates differ only in the order of pronoun and infinitive; ASV's 'many things to say unto you' is compatible with either.

ASV reads 'guide you into all the truth'. 'into' excludes the base's locative en te aletheia ('in all the truth'); the two accusative readings differ only in the position of 'all' and the English does not settle between them.
ASV reads 'what things soever he shall hear', a future; this excludes the present akouei. The future indicative and the an-plus-subjunctive both yield the same English and are not distinguished.
ASV reads 'ye behold me no more'. 'no more' renders ouketi; the bare negative would give 'ye behold me not'.
ASV ends the verse at 'ye shall see me'; the added clause 'because I go to the Father' is absent from v. 16 in the ASV.
ASV's 'Because I go to the Father' supplies 'I' from the first-person verb; the added emphatic pronoun would not change the English.
The candidates differ only in the order of the interrogative and the demonstrative; ASV's 'What is this' is compatible with either.
ASV quotes 'A little while?' directly; an article substantivizing the quoted phrase has no separate English rendering here.

ASV has no connective: 'Jesus perceived that...'. This excludes the added oun, which the ASV renders 'therefore' elsewhere in the context. The presence or absence of the article with the name is not distinguishable in English.
ASV renders the neighbouring de ('but the world shall rejoice') and then gives 'ye shall be sorrowful' with no connective, so the added de is not read.
The candidates differ only in the order of 'now', the particle, and 'sorrow'; ASV's 'ye therefore now have sorrow' is compatible with either.
ASV reads the present 'your joy no one taketh away from you', not the future 'shall take away'.
ASV reads 'If ye shall ask anything of the Father', with no recitative 'that' and the indefinite 'anything'; the alternative's hosa would give 'whatsoever things'.

ASV places the phrase after the giving: 'he will give it you in my name'. The alternative order attaches 'in my name' to the asking, which the ASV does not read. The verse note is an alternative_rendering about 'ask me no question'.
ASV reads 'the hour cometh' with no adversative; the added alla would be rendered 'but'.
Both compounds of the announcing verb yield ASV's 'shall tell you plainly'; the English does not distinguish them. The verse note ('Or, parables') is an alternative_rendering.
ASV reads 'I came forth from the Father', not 'from God'.
Both prepositions are rendered by ASV's 'from' in 'I came out from the Father'; the English does not distinguish them.
ASV reads 'His disciples say, Lo...' with no indirect object; the added 'unto him' is not rendered.
With or without the preposition the phrase is adverbial and ASV renders it 'plainly'; the English does not distinguish them. The verse note ('Or, parable') is an alternative_rendering.
The added article with the name has no separate English rendering; ASV's 'Jesus answered them' is compatible with either.
ASV reads 'yea, is come' with no temporal adverb; the added nun would be rendered 'now'.
